name_en: Nara noppei — a thick vegetable stew made for the Kasuga shrine's December festival
summary_ja: 里芋や大根、ニンジンを昆布と干しシイタケのだしで煮込み、里芋の煮くずれで自然にとろみをつけた奈良の精進煮もの。春日大社のおん祭に先立つ大宿所祭で、大和士や参拝者にふるまわれてきたとされる。
summary_en: A Nara vegetable stew of taro, daikon, and carrot simmered in a kelp-and-dried-shiitake stock, thickened naturally as the taro breaks down — a vegetarian dish. It is said to be served to participants at the Oyadokoro rite that precedes Kasuga Shrine's December festival.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Zuiki no nimono — taro leaf-stalks simmered with fried tofu
summary_ja: 里芋の葉柄であるずいきを薄揚げと一緒にだし汁で煮る奈良の家庭料理。皮をむいてゆでアクを抜いてから使い、乾燥させた「芋がら」として保存することもある。お盆には七色お和えと合わせて仏壇に供える地域もある。
summary_en: A Nara home dish of taro leaf-stalks, called zuiki, simmered with fried tofu in dashi. The stalks are peeled and parboiled to draw out their harshness before use, and are sometimes dried into a preserve called imogara; in some areas it is offered at the household altar for Obon alongside nanairo oae.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Nanairo oae — seven summer vegetables dressed in sesame, miso, and sugar
summary_ja: なす、かぼちゃ、ごぼう、ずいきなど旬の七種の野菜を、すりごまと味噌、砂糖の和え衣で和える真言宗のお盆の供え料理。食糧が乏しかった時代、七種もの野菜をそろえるのは贅沢なことだったという。
summary_en: A Shingon-sect Obon offering dish that dresses seven seasonal vegetables — eggplant, kabocha, burdock, taro-stem, and more — in a coating of ground sesame, miso, and sugar. In leaner times, gathering as many as seven vegetables for one dish is said to have been something of a luxury.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_ja: 大和まなと薄揚げの煮もの
name_en: Yamato-na to usuage no nimono — a local leaf mustard simmered with fried tofu
summary_ja: アブラナ科の伝統野菜、大和まなを薄揚げと炒め煮にする奈良の家庭料理。「古事記」に記される菘（すずな）を祖先とするツケナの一種とされ、霜にあたる冬に甘みが増すが、品種改良で今は通年出回っている。
summary_en: A Nara home dish that stir-simmers yamato-na, a traditional brassica leaf vegetable, with fried tofu. It is said to descend from the leaf vegetable named suzuna in the Kojiki, and grows sweeter after frost in winter, though breeding has since made it available year-round.
source_title: 大和まなと薄揚げの煮もの
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Itadori no nimono — peeled Japanese knotweed stir-fried after a long soak to draw out its sourness
summary_ja: アクと酸味の強い山菜、いたどりの皮をむいて水にさらしてから炒め煮にする吉野山間部の料理。「痛取り」の名は傷にすりこむと痛みが和らぐという言い伝えに由来するとされ、塩漬けにして長く保存もできる。
summary_en: A dish from Nara's Yoshino mountains that peels and soaks Japanese knotweed, a sharply astringent and sour wild green, before stir-frying it. Its name, itadori, is said to come from a belief that rubbing it on a wound eases the pain, and the plant can also be salted for long storage.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Amago no kanroni — river trout simmered slowly in roasted tea and sweet soy
summary_ja: 渓流の女王とも呼ばれるアマゴを素焼きにし、ほうじ茶で煮てから醤油とみりんで甘辛く煮含める吉野郡・宇陀郡の料理。クセのない川魚とされ、古くから家庭で作られてきたおふくろの味という。
summary_en: River trout, called the queen of the mountain stream, first grilled plain and then simmered in roasted tea before being finished sweet and savory in soy sauce and mirin — a dish of the Yoshino and Uda districts. The fish is said to have little of a river-fish's usual edge, and the dish is remembered as a mother's home cooking.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Namabushi to negi no nimono — half-dried bonito simmered with sweet local scallions
summary_ja: カツオ節の製造途中で燻し上げた生節を、結崎ネブカなど地元のねぎと一緒に濃いめの醤油だしで煮る奈良の料理。海に面さない奈良では日持ちする生節が重宝され、ねぎとの組み合わせがよく食べられてきたとされる。
summary_en: Half-smoked bonito, an intermediate stage in making dried bonito flakes, simmered in a strong soy dashi with local scallions such as Kawanishi's Yuzaki negi. Landlocked Nara is said to have long valued the fish for how well it keeps, and its pairing with scallion is a common combination.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Ei no nikogori — stingray simmered sweet and soy until its own gelatin sets into a jelly
summary_ja: 赤エイを醤油と砂糖で甘辛く煮つけた奈良の料理。ゼラチン質が煮汁に溶け出し、冷めるとゼリー状に固まることから「煮こごり」と呼ばれる。春日大社若宮のおん祭では、のっぺいと共に食べられてきたとされる。
summary_en: Red stingray simmered sweet and savory in soy sauce and sugar, a Nara dish. Its own gelatin dissolves into the cooking liquid and sets into a jelly once cooled, giving the dish its name, nikogori. It is said to have been eaten together with noppei at Kasuga Shrine's Wakamiya festival.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
